- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.4), model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast upward slightly to avoid excessive sell-off bias.  
- After sharp price spikes, model often overshoots downward in subsequent periods; apply a mild upward bias to counteract lagged sell pressure.  
- If recent history shows mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive downward moves), model may underestimate rebound; add a small upward adjustment to capture momentum.  
- When sentiment is mildly positive (e.g., 0.0 to +0.3), model often underestimates upward movement; increase forecast slightly to reflect bullish sentiment.  
- For 30-day horizon, model frequently underestimates true price in early periods (e.g., first 5–7 days); apply a small upward bias to the initial forecast points.  
- If sentiment history shows recent volatility (e.g., alternating +/– values), model tends to smooth too much; allow for more jagged, sentiment-aligned adjustments.
